hints: A graph of $y=|f(x)|$ is obtained by reflecting any part of $y=f(x)$ below the $x$-axis upwards.
Find where $2x+1=0$ to locate the vertex of the V-shaped graph.
Use the slopes of $2x+1$ on the right and its reflection on the left, and mark the value when $x=0$.
walkthrough:
Find the vertex of the graph where the argument of the modulus is zero:
$$2x + 1 = 0 \implies 2x = -1 \implies x = -\dfrac{1}{2}$$
At this point, $y = |0| = 0$, giving the vertex at $\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}, 0\right)$.

Find the $y$-intercept by substituting $x = 0$:
$$y = |2(0) + 1| = |1| = 1$$
This gives the point $(0, 1)$ on the $y$-axis.

Identify the two linear branches forming the V-shaped graph:
For $x \geq -\dfrac{1}{2}$: $y = 2x + 1$ (a straight line of gradient $+2$ through $(0, 1)$).
For $x < -\dfrac{1}{2}$: $y = -(2x + 1) = -2x - 1$ (a straight line of gradient $-2$).
Sketch the complete graph showing a V-shape with vertex at $\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}, 0\right)$ and crossing the $y$-axis at $(0, 1)$.

$$3x + 5 < 2x + 1$$
